title: Constructed ring comparison for the middle closed-fibre colimit
statement: Let X be a Noetherian local model tower [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-model-tower] over a local ring R, with its explicit middle closed-fibre functor A [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-model-tower-fiber-system]. Define the cocone to ULift(S/m_R S) by descending the stage limit maps. Its underlying maps are jointly surjective and equality of two quotient classes at a stage descends to equality at a later stage. This makes it a colimit cocone and defines its canonical comparison ring equivalence fiberAEquiv from colimit A to S/m_R S. Every definition has constructed data or data determined uniquely by a proved colimit universal property; no unproved theorem is used.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 00R7, paragraph beginning with the colimit of the maximal ideals, quotient systems before the second use of Tag 00R6; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00R7.

proof.text: The images of stage extended maximal ideals form an ideal in S: move summands and multipliers to a common stage using directedness and slimit_surj. It contains the image of the maximal ideal of R. Indeed rlimit_surj lifts each coefficient, and a unit lift would have a unit image. Hence every element of m_R S comes from a stage ideal.

Descend the stage limit maps through the quotients and compose with ULift.up to construct a cocone. Quotient representatives prove naturality. Every quotient class is represented at a stage by slimit_surj. For equality of two stage classes, their difference lies in m_R S; represent that ideal element at a common stage and use slimit_eq at a further stage to show the difference lies in its stage ideal. Types.FilteredColimit.isColimitOf' proves the underlying cocone colimiting; reflection by forget CommRingCat proves the ring cocone colimiting. Its unique comparison with colimit A, followed by ULift.ringEquiv, constructs fiberAEquiv.

proof_origin.note: Completely proved quotient representative and eventual-equality construction.

A directed system of local ring quotients and modules has colimit the quotient by the maximal ideal
